## [[Biznezz Cardz!!]{.cards}](https://github.com/rstudio/pagedown#business-cards-pagedownbusiness_card)

::: {.panel-tabset}

### pagedown {{< iconify emojione-v1:note-page >}}

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}

````{r}
---
phone: "+1 844-448-1212"
email: "info@posit.co"
url: www.homehere.com
address: |
  Minneapolis, MN
logo: "logo.png"
person: 
  - name: John Kulas
    title: Janitor of All Messy
    repeat: 12
googlefonts: "`Pinyon Script`" # feel free to try other fonts at https://fonts.google.com
paperwidth: 8.5in
paperheight: 11in
cols: 4
rows: 3
output: pagedown::business_card
knit: pagedown::chrome_print          #<1>
---

<!-- if you prefer you can create cards in markdown instead of YAML declaration -->

```{css}                           #<2>
.me {
    font-size: 16px;
    letter-spacing: 0.8px;
    line-height: 1.7em;
    padding: 0.4cm;
}                                  #<2>

```
<!-- if you prefer black text on white background, set eval=TRUE on the chunk below 
-->

```{css, eval=FALSE}               #<3>
.wrapper {
  color: black;
  background-color: white;
  border: 4px dotted black;
}
.coordinates {
  color: #333;
}
```                               #<3>

````
1. `pagedown::chrome_print` will create .pdf representations of the focal .html file
2. [We]{.underline} wrote this to exert some control over font size within individual cards 
3. [`pagedown`]{.underline} authors included this in template (you can activate by changing chunk command to `eval=TRUE`)
:::

### $\LaTeX$ {{< iconify skill-icons:latex-light >}}

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

```{r}
---
title: ""
format:
  pdf:
    documentclass: article
    geometry:                 #<1>
      - paperwidth=3.5in
      - paperheight=2in
      - margin=0.15in         #<1>
    pagestyle: empty
---

**I.M. Fancy**  
Data Scientist

jenny@TuTone.com  
+1 657 5309
```
1. control card size & margin width here -- [geometry](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/pdf-basics.html#output-options) works well 

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

<br>
Professional printshops likely want the entire card specified in one .pdf (rather than multiple cards repeated on one page)

:::
